candidates.label: Acute exogenous bacterial endophthalmitis of the left eye due to Streptococcus intermedius, likely post-dental procedure
missing_or_uncertain: Posterior segment unremarkable may be early or limited anterior involvement

candidates.label: Bacterial keratitis with hypopyon (corneal ulcer) due to Streptococcus intermedius
missing_or_uncertain: Granuloma not typical for bacterial keratitis; dental cleaning less relevant

candidates.label: Endogenous bacterial endophthalmitis due to Streptococcus intermedius
missing_or_uncertain: Source of bacteremia not identified; dental cleaning suggests exogenous route

candidates.label: Severe anterior uveitis with hypopyon (non-infectious inflammatory)
missing_or_uncertain: Positive culture and gram stain argue against non-infectious etiology

candidates.label: Fungal endophthalmitis
missing_or_uncertain: Gram stain and culture indicate bacteria, not fungi

response.rationale: The acute presentation with pain, hypopyon, granuloma, and positive culture for Streptococcus intermedius after dental cleaning strongly supports exogenous bacterial endophthalmitis. The unremarkable posterior segment does not exclude early endophthalmitis. Keratitis and uveitis are less consistent with the culture and granuloma.
